subject.title: Discord account-to-agent routing falls back to default agent instead of matching by account name

question: Should Discord multi-account routing add a guarded same-name accountId-to-agent fallback after explicit binding tiers miss, or should explicit bindings remain the only supported account-to-agent contract?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but fallback semantics affect security, provider/model routing, and session ownership for existing Discord multi-account setups.

options.title: Approve Guarded Discord Fallback
options.body: Route a non-default Discord accountId to an existing same-named configured agent only after explicit binding tiers miss, with diagnostics, docs, regression tests, and live Discord proof.

options.title: Keep Explicit Bindings Only
options.body: Leave runtime fallback unchanged and add docs, doctor, or status warnings for Discord accounts that look intended to bind to same-named agents.

options.title: Repair The Fork PR First
options.body: Use the linked fork PR as source material only after conflicts, agent-existence guards, diagnostics, and real Discord proof are addressed.

recommendation.title: Approve Guarded Discord Fallback
recommendation.body: Route a non-default Discord accountId to an existing same-named configured agent only after explicit binding tiers miss, with diagnostics, docs, regression tests, and live Discord proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current history signal across shared routing, Discord route-resolution, docs, and prior routing hardening points to steipete for the product/security decision.
